note: Load test: can public HTTP traffic starve the executor? Driven against a local instance while a real Coston2 instruction was in flight, so the answer is measured against the thing that actually matters -- whether the instruction still executed, and on time.
why: The status routes share a process, an event loop and an upstream rate limit with the watch, attest and execute loop. Sharing an upstream budget is the part that does not show up in a latency graph: before this, a /status lookup spent the same ~20 DA Layer requests a minute the executor needs to fetch proofs, so enough public traffic would have stopped execution while every health signal stayed green.

mitigations.splitDaBudget: 3/4 of the DA Layer allowance to the executor (blocking), 1/4 to public lookups (non-blocking). A lookup with no token skips the proof search and answers from the chain alone, which the classifier already reports honestly as 'no proof in the scanned window'.
mitigations.globalRateLimit: 300/min across all callers, so a forged x-forwarded-for spreads a caller across buckets without raising the total
mitigations.lookupConcurrencyCap: 10 /status lookups in flight; further ones get 429 immediately rather than queueing behind chain reads
mitigations.caching: /instructions and /metrics cached 5s and served with Cache-Control: max-age=5

executorUnderLoad.verdict: no degradation: 132 s under load against a 159 s unloaded baseline. The difference is voting-round alignment, not load.

loopHealth.verdict: the loop never stalled: 15.4 s per tick against a 15 s target while absorbing 52,274 requests a second

whatBound: All 6.27M requests came from one address, so the per-IP bucket bound, not the global one: 10 burst + 30/min over two minutes = ~70, and 69 were served. The global cap is what bounds a caller who forges the key across many buckets.
honestly: Peak latency was 6,562 ms on one request. That is a /status lookup that had already passed the limiter and was waiting on chain reads while the RPC was busy; it is bounded by the concurrency cap rather than by the rate limit, and it delayed nobody but that caller.
